All work
Mobile app · 2025

HayWay

A modern and user-friendly taxi app designed to solve real rider frustrations, from payment confusion to ride scheduling. A complete case study, from user research and usability testing to the final interface.

RoleEnd-to-end UX/UI
PlatformiOS · Android
YearJune 2025
ToolsFigma · Miro
Full case on Behance
Overview

A taxi app that stays clear at every step of the ride

Riders in Armenia told the same story: prices that change at the last moment, payments that are hard to understand, an awkward conversation every time a fare has to be split, and no simple way to order a car for later.

HayWay is a ride-hailing concept for the Armenian market that answers those problems directly. I took it from the first interview to a tested, high-fidelity prototype built on a reusable component library.

Process
01Research

Competitive research of the ride-hailing apps people already use, plus quantitative and qualitative research with riders.

02Define

User personas, customer journey mapping and affinity mapping showed where trips go wrong. Feature prioritisation turned the findings into the MVP scope.

03Design

User flows, low-fidelity wireframes, then usability testing and iteration before any visual polish.

04Deliver

High-fidelity screens and an interactive prototype, built on a reusable component library so new flows stay consistent.

Highlights
Transparent pricing

The fare is visible before the ride is confirmed, so there are no surprises at the end of the trip.

Shared fares

Riders can split the cost of a trip inside the app instead of settling it in the car.

Booking rides for future

Schedule a trip ahead of time and travel stress-free, a feature the research showed riders were missing.

Fast pick-up

A map-first home with “From?” and “Where to?” fields gets a rider from opening the app to a booked car in a few taps.

Details
Key screens
  1. 01Onboarding
  2. 02Booking rides for future
  3. 03Map with pick-up and destination
  4. 04Ride booking
  5. 05Shared fare
  6. 06Sign in

E-commerce website · 2024

Skatey

An online store for all things ice skating. Skatey is built so that beginners and experienced skaters both find the right skates and accessories quickly, on desktop and on the phone.

RoleUX research · UI
PlatformWeb · Mobile web
YearJuly 2024
ToolsFigma · Notion
Full case on Behance
Overview

Ice skates, easy to choose for anyone

Buying skates online is hard for beginners and slow for pros. Stores show long lists of similar models, sizes are confusing and the right accessories are scattered across the catalogue.

Skatey is a store concept that offers high-quality skates and accessories to help people skate with style and confidence. The goal was simple browsing and a short path to checkout.

Process
01Research

Market and competitor analysis of skating and sports stores to see how they present products and where they lose people.

02Define

Personas for a beginner and an experienced skater, and journey maps from first visit to purchase.

03Structure

Clear category navigation: Products, Accessories, Sales and Support, with search, cart and sign-in always one tap away.

04Design

Desktop and mobile layouts, prototypes and a flexible design system for future pages.

Highlights
“Everything, just for you”

A bold storefront with a large wordmark and a seasonal hero that puts the new collection first.

New arrivals

The Winter 2024 collection gets its own carousel with a direct “Go to shop” action.

Filters on mobile

Filter chips such as Featured and Man narrow the catalogue without leaving the page.

Clear deals

Product cards show the discount, the old and new price, and a direct “Buy now”.

Details
Key screens
  1. 01Home
  2. 02New arrivals
  3. 03Catalogue
  4. 04Mobile catalogue with filters
  5. 05Product card
  6. 06Cart

News app · redesign · 2024

Meduza

Instant updates, breaking news. A full redesign of the Meduza news app and website, focused on making it calmer and easier to read.

RoleUX/UI redesign
PlatformMobile · Web
YearJanuary 2024
ToolsFigma
Full case on Behance
Overview

All of Meduza in one calm place

Meduza publishes much more than news: podcasts, audiobooks, stories and books. In the current product these live in different places, and a busy feed makes it hard to scan what matters today.

The redesign concept brings everything into one structure that works the same way on the phone and on the web, in a dark interface with a single amber accent.

Process
01Audit

Reviewed the existing app and site and listed every content type and where readers look for it.

02Structure

Top navigation for each content type: Audiobooks, About Meduza, News, Podcasts, Stories and Books.

03Home

A home page built from two blocks: “News today”, all the latest news in one place, and “Blitz news”, short news for a quick read.

04Interface

A calm dark UI with one amber accent, readable cards and the same components across mobile and web.

Highlights
News today

Large cards with an image, headline, short summary, publish time and a bookmark.

Blitz news

Short traditional news for readers who want the headlines in a minute.

Podcasts

A podcast library on mobile with covers, the number of episodes and a quick “Listen”.

Simple tab bar

Home, Favorite, Saved and Settings keep the mobile app easy to move around.

Details
Key screens
  1. 01Web home
  2. 02News today
  3. 03Blitz news
  4. 04Podcasts on mobile
  5. 05Saved
  6. 06Settings

ISAA

Designing public digital services for the Informational Systems Agency of Armenia, used across the country, and working on Henaket, the design system for Armenian government services.

RoleUI/UX Designer
PlatformWeb · Mobile

Overview

Public services that work for everyone

ISAA builds the digital services that people across Armenia use to deal with the state. The work has to be clear for every citizen and consistent across many products and teams.

I work in the agency’s UI/UX Department on the Henaket design system and on the products built with it, and I review existing government websites against the system.

Process
01Henaket

Building Figma components and templates for the Henaket design system, and fixing existing ones.

02Updates

Contributed to two major Henaket updates that product teams now build on.

03Products

Designing and improving Hartak.am, including MyData and the feedback section, and pages of the Hartak mobile app. Designed the Azdarar website.

04Audits

More than 30 manual website audits, almost all of them government sites, covering design-system compliance and quality.

Highlights
Henaket components

Reusable Figma components and templates that keep government services consistent.

Hartak.am

Improvements to the public portal, including MyData and a feedback section.

Azdarar

Design of the Azdarar website.

e-draft

Helped the e-draft team with design and took part in meetings on improving the product.

Bizzy Agency

The full Bizzy Agency website and its complete admin panel, designed on one shared component system so both stay consistent.

RoleUI/UX Designer
PlatformWeb · Admin
SinceJuly 2025

Overview

Data-driven marketing, creative by design

Bizzy is a digital marketing agency that crafts identities and marketing strategies for brands, from strategy to execution.

I designed the public website with a modern UI, a clean visual identity and a conversion-minded structure, and the complete admin panel the team uses to run it.

Process
01Website

The full agency website: Home, About Us, Projects, Services and Contact Us, with clear calls to action.

02Identity

A deep purple base with bright pink and yellow accents and the bee mark, so the brand is recognisable on every page.

03Admin panel

The complete admin interface, including data-dense views and responsive layouts.

04System

One scalable component system shared by the marketing site and the admin product.

Highlights
Hero with two paths

“View Projects” and “Our Services” send visitors straight to proof or to the offer.

About Us

“Your brand, our passion” explains who the agency is and how it works with clients.

Data-dense admin

Tables and views that handle a lot of data and still work on smaller screens.

Shared components

The site and the admin use the same buttons, cards and forms.
